title: Change default username and password
description: Extreme switches have a default username and password. These need to be changed from their default values.
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.2.1 Change default username and password

audit.command: Run 'show running-config | include username' and confirm the default 'admin' and 'user' accounts have had their passwords changed (or have been replaced by named accounts) and that no account still uses the factory default password ('password').

remediation.command:
configure terminal
username admin password <new-strong-password> role admin
username user password <new-strong-password> role user
end
(or create named accounts and remove the defaults)

title: Ensure Password complexity is configured
description: It is prudent to use a minimum length to 14 characters. Maximum length should be as long as possible based on system constraints PASS requires password-attributes min-length >= 8, max-retry <= 4 and character-restriction upper >= 1, lower >= 2, numeric >= 1 and special-char >= 1 (the CIS values), matched in the order SLX-OS prints them. Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.2.2 Ensure Password complexity is configured

remediation.command:
configure terminal
password-attributes min-length 8
password-attributes max-retry 4
password-attributes character-restriction upper 1
password-attributes character-restriction lower 2
password-attributes character-restriction numeric 1
password-attributes character-restriction special-char 1
end
# CIS guidance:
password-attributes min-length 8
password-attributes max-retry 4
password-attributes character-restriction upper 1
password-attributes character-restriction lower 2
password-attributes character-restriction numeric 1
password-attributes character-restriction special-char 1

title: Ensure system is running TLS 1.2 or later
description: Ensuring secure data transmission is crucial in our digital age. TLS 1.2 stands out by offering advanced encryption algorithms, improved key exchange mechanisms, and enhanced protection against known vulnerabilities. This level of security ensures the privacy and integrity of sensitive information transmitted over the internet. As a result, most modern browsers and services now mandate the use of TLS 1.2 or higher for secure connections. PASS requires the management-security server SSL profile to set tls min-version 1.2 (or 1.3); also check the client profile. Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.3.1 Ensure system is running TLS 1.2 or later

remediation.command:
configure terminal
management-security
 ssl-profile server
  tls min-version 1.2
 !
 ssl-profile client
  tls min-version 1.2
end

title: Enable NTP Server Authentication
description: The switch should be synchronized with NTP server with authentication turned on. Authenticating to the NTP servers prevent an adversary from spoofing the NTP address and establishing connection. PASS requires ntp authenticate (with trusted ntp authentication keys on the servers). Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.4.2 Enable NTP Server Authentication

remediation.command:
configure terminal
ntp authentication-key 1 sha1 <key>
ntp server 192.168.0.10 key 1
ntp authenticate
end
# CIS guidance:
Configure the NTP Server configuration and authentication
ntp authenticate

title: Enable Local Login Authentication
description: Enabling local login authentication in AAA (Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting) allows a system to authenticate users using a local database instead of relying on an external server like RADIUS or TACACS+. Here's how it works: Local User Database: The system uses its own local database to store usernames and passwords. Authentication Process: When a user attempts to log in, the system checks the local database for the credentials. Fallback Option: It can be used as a fallback method if the external authentication server is unavailable. This setup is useful as a backup method to ensure users can still authenticate even if the external server is down. PASS requires aaa authentication login local. Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.6.1 Enable Local Login Authentication

remediation.command:
configure terminal
aaa authentication login local
end
# CIS guidance:
aaa authentication login local

title: Ensure the system is on a supported Network Operating System
description: Extreme Networks releases software releases periodically to close defects, upgrade security postures, and close security vulnerabilities. Customers are expected to be utilizing a supported software release.
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.1 Ensure the system is on a supported Network Operating System

audit.command: Run 'show version | include SLX-OS' and confirm the running SLX-OS release is a currently supported 20.x release per Extreme Networks' end-of-support notices, with the latest maintenance patch applied.

remediation.command: Update to the latest stable release

title: Ensure multiple NTP servers are configured
description: NTP servers ensure that the system maintains the correct time to prevent drift and delays. If an adversary gains access to an NTP server it is more difficult to cause issues if there are multiple servers configured on the device PASS requires at least two ntp server lines. Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.4.1 Ensure multiple NTP servers are configured

remediation.command:
configure terminal
ntp server 192.168.0.10 source-interface-type management source-interface-number 0
ntp server 192.168.0.11 source-interface-type management source-interface-number 0
end
# CIS guidance:
ntp server 192.168.0.10 source-interface-type management source-
interface-number 0

title: Syslog Server Configuration
description: Switches should have a syslog server configuration to enable the syslog logging activity to function. PASS requires a syslog server. Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.5.1 Syslog Server Configuration

remediation.command:
configure terminal
logging syslog-server 192.168.0.10 use-vrf mgmt-vrf source-interface management 0
end
# CIS guidance:
logging syslog-server 192.168.0.10 use-vrf mgmt-vrf source-
interface management 0

title: Syslog Facility Configuration
description: Switches should have a syslog server configuration to enable the syslog logging activity to function. PASS requires a local syslog facility (the CIS example uses LOG_LOCAL7). Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.5.2 Syslog Facility Configuration

remediation.command:
configure terminal
logging syslog-facility local LOG_LOCAL7
end
# CIS guidance:
logging syslog-facility local LOG_LOCAL7

title: Syslog Audit Class Configuration
description: A syslog audit class is a categorization mechanism used in logging systems to classify and group different types of audit events. This allows administrators to define what specific events or activities should be logged. PASS requires auditlog classes SECURITY, CONFIGURATION and FIRMWARE. Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.5.3 Syslog Audit Class Configuration

audit.pattern: (?m)(?:^logging auditlog class SECURITY\b(?s:.*?)^logging auditlog class CONFIGURATION\b(?s:.*?)^logging auditlog class FIRMWARE\b|^logging auditlog class SECURITY\b(?s:.*?)^logging auditlog class FIRMWARE\b(?s:.*?)^logging auditlog class CONFIGURATION\b|^logging auditlog class CONFIGURATION\b(?s:.*?)^logging auditlog class SECURITY\b(?s:.*?)^logging auditlog class FIRMWARE\b|^logging auditlog class CONFIGURATION\b(?s:.*?)^logging auditlog class FIRMWARE\b(?s:.*?)^logging auditlog class SECURITY\b|^logging auditlog class FIRMWARE\b(?s:.*?)^logging auditlog class SECURITY\b(?s:.*?)^logging auditlog class CONFIGURATION\b|^logging auditlog class FIRMWARE\b(?s:.*?)^logging auditlog class CONFIGURATION\b(?s:.*?)^logging auditlog class SECURITY\b)

remediation.command:
configure terminal
logging auditlog class SECURITY
logging auditlog class CONFIGURATION
logging auditlog class FIRMWARE
end
# CIS guidance:
logging auditlog class SECURITY
logging auditlog class CONFIGURATION
logging auditlog class FIRMWARE

title: Enable Accounting
description: AAA accounting, a crucial component of the AAA framework, stands for Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting. Here's a breakdown of what AAA accounting entails: Tracking User Activities: AAA accounting monitors and records user activities on a network, such as login attempts, resource access, and changes to system configurations. Usage Auditing: It helps in auditing the usage of network resources by keeping detailed logs of user interactions with the system, which can be vital for both security and performance analysis. PASS requires exec and command accounting (aaa accounting exec/commands default start-stop). Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.6.2 Enable Accounting

audit.pattern: (?m)(?:^aaa accounting exec default start-stop\b(?s:.*?)^aaa accounting commands default start-stop\b|^aaa accounting commands default start-stop\b(?s:.*?)^aaa accounting exec default start-stop\b)

remediation.command:
configure terminal
aaa accounting exec default start-stop tacacs+
aaa accounting commands default start-stop tacacs+
end
# CIS guidance:
aaa authentication login local
aaa accounting exec default start-stop none
aaa accounting commands default start-stop none
aaa authorization command none

title: Disable Unused Interfaces
description: Any unused interface should be disabled. The SLX-OS switches enable all ports by default. However, unused ports should be disabled and only used ports should be enabled.
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 3.1.1 Disable Unused Interfaces

audit.command: Run 'show interface status' (e.g. 'show interface status | include Eth.*Down | count') and confirm every Ethernet port that is not connected or not in use is administratively shut down.

title: Disable Proxy Arp
description: Proxy ARP (Proxy Address Resolution Protocol) is a network technique that allows one device on a local network to respond to ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) requests on behalf of another device While Proxy ARP can be useful, it also has some drawbacks: Security Risks: It can potentially expose the network to security risks, such as ARP spoofing and man-in-the-middle attacks. Network Performance: It can introduce additional traffic on the network, which may impact performance.
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 3.1.2 Disable Proxy Arp

audit.command: Run 'show running-config interface' and confirm no Layer 3 interface (ve, ethernet) has 'ip proxy-arp' configured; proxy ARP must stay disabled unless explicitly required.

remediation.command:
configure terminal
interface ve <id>
 no ip proxy-arp
end
(note: the CIS text for this item repeats the 'Disable Unused Interfaces' commands)

title: Ensure BGP Configuration
description: BGP, or Border Gateway Protocol, is a standardized exterior gateway protocol used to exchange routing information between different autonomous systems (AS) on the internet. PASS requires a router bgp configuration (only applicable where the switch runs BGP). Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 4.1.1 Ensure BGP Configuration

remediation.command:
configure terminal
router bgp
end
write memory
# CIS guidance:
router bgp
write

title: Ensure AS number configuration
description: A BGP AS number (ASN), or Autonomous System Number, is a unique identifier assigned to each autonomous system (AS) on the internet. PASS requires a local-as number in router bgp. Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 4.1.2 Ensure AS number configuration

remediation.command:
configure terminal
router bgp
 local-as 65512
 capability as4-enable
 fast-external-fallover
end
# CIS guidance:
router bgp
local-as 65512
capability as4-enable
fast-external-fallover
end

title: Check V3 host configuration
description: SNMPv3 (Simple Network Management Protocol version 3) is the latest version of SNMP, designed to provide secure access to devices by incorporating robust security features PASS requires an SNMPv3 host (snmp-server v3host). Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 5.1.1 Check V3 host configuration

remediation.command:
configure terminal
snmp-server v3host 10.18.120.110 efav3User
end
# CIS guidance:
snmp-server v3host 10.18.120.110 efav3User

title: Configure Host Name
description: Extreme Networks switches ship with a default host name. The host-name property should be set up to be unique name on the management network. This enables the switch to be resolved with a unique FQDN. PASS requires switch-attributes host-name set to a name other than the default 'SLX'. Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.2 Configure Host Name

remediation.command:
configure terminal
switch-attributes host-name <new_switch>
end
# CIS guidance:
config terminal
switch-attributes host-name new_switch
end

title: Ensure that the Default Chassis Name is changed
description: It is incredibly important to change default ID's to ensure that they are not easily compromised from an attacker. FAILs if the chassis name is still the factory model name (SLXnnnn...). Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 1.3 Ensure that the Default Chassis Name is changed

remediation.command:
configure terminal
switch-attributes chassis-name <new_chassis_name>
end
# CIS guidance:
config terminal
switch-attributes chassis-name new_switch
end

title: Login Banner
description: An approved use notification, in the form of a Login Banner, should be displayed before granting access to the switch. Such a banner ensures that the privacy and security notification verbiage used is consistent with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidance. PASS requires a login banner. Audited against SLX-OS 'show running-config' output (saved in full).
reference: CIS ExtremeNetworks SLX-OS 20.X.X Benchmark v1.0.1 - 2.1.1 Login Banner

remediation.command:
configure terminal
banner login "Authorized access only. Activity is monitored."
end
# CIS guidance:
banner login "Please do not disturb the setup on this switch"
